lead.zh-Hans: 等人的时候，海面替我换了好几次背景。
lead.en: While I waited, the sea kept changing the backdrop.

text.zh-Hans: 到了釜山，我在广安里海边等一位同行的旅人，远处是广安大桥。对方来了，我们没有立刻走，先各说一件等候时看到的小事。我说海面亮了一小块，对方说刚才一路都在找我那只邮包。于是我在便签上画了邮包和一条浪，给这次碰面添了两个记号。
text.en: At Gwangalli Beach in Busan, I waited for a fellow traveler with Gwangandaegyo Bridge in view. Once together, we each described a small thing from the wait. I had noticed a bright patch of water; my companion had spent the walk looking for my mailbag. A bag and a wave went onto my note, two signs for a successful meeting.

text.zh-Hans: 接着聊聊路上看到的小事
text.en: Keep trading small things seen along the way

text.zh-Hans: 记下海面亮起的那一小块
text.en: Remember the bright patch on the water

lead.zh-Hans: 今天，我站在能看海的地方，听了好一会儿。
lead.en: Today I gave the sea a long listening turn.

text.zh-Hans: 在釜山太宗台的观景处，我看着层层岩石旁的海浪。这里能见到海蚀崖等地貌，我没有急着把名词都记下来，先听了一会儿浪声。写便签时，每句话后面都不自觉空得很长。我决定保留这些空白，让纸上的海也有时间再响一次。
text.en: At a lookout in Taejongdae, Busan, I watched waves beside the layered rocks and sea cliffs. Instead of trying to collect every geological term, I listened for a while. My notes came out with unusually long spaces after each sentence. I left them there, giving the sea on the page time for another turn.

text.zh-Hans: 给这段浪声取个短标题
text.en: Choose a short title for the waves

text.zh-Hans: 听听两阵浪之间的空隙
text.en: Listen to the interval between waves

lead.zh-Hans: 一碗凉面，把午后的语速也放慢了。
lead.en: A cool bowl slowed my afternoon sentences.

text.zh-Hans: 我在釜山尝了小麦冷面，小麦面条浸在冷肉汤里。吃的时候没有急着写菜单，等放下筷子，才把那股凉意记在卡片上。想形容得准确一点，最后却只写下“慢慢吃完的一碗”。这句话留给我自己读，旁边再添一个小碗就够了。
text.en: In Busan I tried milmyeon, wheat noodles in cold meat broth. I waited until the chopsticks were down before writing the menu card. Searching for a precise description of that cool bowl, I settled on “a bowl I took my time over.” A note for my own memory, with a small bowl beside it.

text.zh-Hans: 找一个词记下这股凉意
text.en: Choose a word for that coolness

text.zh-Hans: 回想碗里最先注意到的部分
text.en: Recall what first caught your eye in the bowl

lead.zh-Hans: 今天的小菜单，借了一把汤匙当标点。
lead.en: A spoon became today’s menu punctuation.

text.zh-Hans: 在釜山吃猪肉汤饭，猪肉、汤和米饭让这一顿很踏实。饭后写菜单，我把汤匙画在菜名后面，弯弯的柄看起来像一个问号。我本来想擦掉，后来决定留下：它问的也许只是“还记得这一碗吗”。把卡片夹进本子之前，我点了点头。
text.en: Pork, broth and rice made a comfortable meal of dwaeji gukbap in Busan. Afterwards I drew a spoon after the dish name on my menu. Its curved handle looked like a question mark. I nearly erased it, then let it ask a simple question: “Remember this bowl?” I nodded before putting the card away.

text.zh-Hans: 替汤匙写一个小问题
text.en: Write a small question for the spoon

text.zh-Hans: 看看汤匙最像哪个标点
text.en: Decide which punctuation mark the spoon resembles

lead.zh-Hans: 聊起今天，两张菜单替我接了两次话。
lead.en: Two menu cards helped me tell the day’s story.

text.zh-Hans: 今天在釜山，我午间尝了小麦冷面，另一顿吃了猪肉汤饭。遇到一位旅人问我过得怎样，我就拿出两张菜单：一张写“凉”，一张画了汤匙。对方说这封信开头像午饭，结尾像晚饭。我把两张卡排好，觉得中间还该夹一句“出去走了走”。
text.en: Today in Busan, I had milmyeon at lunch and dwaeji gukbap at another meal. When a traveler asked about my day, I showed two cards: one said “cool,” the other carried a spoon. My account apparently began like lunch and ended like dinner. I put the cards in order and considered adding, “Went for a walk in between.”

text.zh-Hans: 把两顿饭之间的散步讲完
text.en: Tell the walk between the meals

text.zh-Hans: 看看两张卡各留下了什么
text.en: Look at what each card kept

lead.zh-Hans: 同一天里，我记住了一凉一暖。
lead.en: One day left me a cool memory and a warm one.

text.zh-Hans: 在釜山，我分两次尝了小麦冷面和猪肉汤饭，各写一张小菜单。收卡片时，它们摸起来都是纸的温度，想到的却一个凉、一个暖。我试着用手掌盖住标题，只看旁边留下的词和汤匙画。没有猜错，今天的两顿饭还认得回来。
text.en: I tried milmyeon and dwaeji gukbap at separate meals in Busan and made a menu for each. Packed away, both cards felt like ordinary paper, yet one brought back coolness and the other warmth. I covered the titles with my palm and used the words and spoon drawing as clues. Both meals found their way back.

text.zh-Hans: 请旅人猜猜两张卡是哪道菜
text.en: Invite a traveler to guess the two dishes

text.zh-Hans: 遮住标题再看一次记号
text.en: Cover the titles and study the clues again

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，我把海边那一点亮光留进了信里。
lead.en: “{reply}” gave the bright patch of sea a place in my letter.

text.zh-Hans: 广安里海边等人时看到的亮光，我用淡淡一圈铅笔留在卡片上，又添了当时远远望见的桥。这里没有准确的距离，只记得人到齐以后，我们还舍不得立刻走。我把碰面的两个小记号折进卡片里面，等收信的人打开，才让邮包和那条浪一起露面。
text.en: I kept the bright patch from my Gwangalli wait as a faint pencil ring and added the distant bridge. The distances are not exact; I mainly remember that even after meeting up, we lingered. I folded the two meeting signs inside the card. When someone opens it, the mailbag and the wave can appear together.

text.zh-Hans: 给卡片里的邮包写句问候
text.en: Write a greeting for the mailbag inside

text.zh-Hans: 找找淡淡的亮光圆圈
text.en: Find the faint ring of light
